metadata.title: A DYNAMICAL APPROACH TO AN INERTIAL FORWARD-BACKWARD ALGORITHM FOR CONVEX MINIMIZATION

items.name: Hypothesis H
items.statement:
Hypothesis $H$ .

$H_{\Phi}$ : The function $\Phi: H \to \mathbf{R} \cup \{+\infty\}$ is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex.

$H_{\Psi}$ : The function $\Psi : H \to \mathbf{R}$ is differentiable and its gradient $\nabla \Psi$ is Lipschitz continuous with constant $L_{\Psi}$ .

$H_{\lambda}$ : The step size $\lambda$ satisfies $0 < \lambda < \Lambda = \min \left\{\frac{1}{a}, \frac{2(a + b)}{bL_{\Psi}}\right\}$ with $a, b > 0$ .

$H_{\Theta}$ : The function $\Theta = \Phi + \Psi$ is convex and bounded from below.
items.remark: [Note: package $H_\Phi,H_\Psi,H_\lambda,H_\Theta$ as a reusable Lean structure] | [Foundation: Foundation.Analysis.ExtendedRealFunctions] recall IsProper

items.name: Velocity sequence $\xi_k$
items.statement:
The velocity of the system is represented by the sequence $(\xi_{k})$ defined by

$$
\xi_ {k} = u _ {k} - u _ {k - 1}.
$$

\zeta_ {k} = y _ {k} - y _ {k - 1} \tag {3.3}

items.name: Lemma 5
items.statement:
LEMMA 5. Let $(a_k)$ , $(b_k)$ , and $(\varepsilon_k)$ be real sequences with $(\varepsilon_k) \in \ell^1$ . Let $\theta \in \mathbf{R}$ and assume

$$
a _ {k} - a _ {k - 1} \leq \theta + \varepsilon_ {k}, \quad b _ {k + 1} - b _ {k} \leq a _ {k}, \quad a n d \quad b _ {k} \geq 0
$$

for all $k \geq k_0$ . Then $\theta \geq 0$ .
items.proof:
Proof. Summing up the first inequality for $k = k_0, \ldots, m$ we deduce that $a_m \leq m\theta + A$ for some constant $A$ . [One may take $A=a_{k_0-1}-k_0\theta+\sum_{j=k_0}^{\infty}|\varepsilon_j|$, because partial sums of the $\ell^1$ sequence are uniformly bounded.] Using the second inequality and summing again for $m = k_0, \ldots, M$ we obtain

$$
b _ {M + 1} - b _ {k _ {0}} \leq \sum_ {k = k _ {0}} ^ {M} a _ {k} \leq \sum_ {k = 1} ^ {M} (k \theta + A) = \frac {M (M + 1)}{2} \theta + M A.
$$

Thus $0 \leq 2b_{M+1} \leq M^2\theta + (2A + \theta)M + 2b_{k_0}$ . Divide by $M^2$ and let $M \to +\infty$ to see that $\theta \geq 0$ . [If $\theta<0$, the right-hand side divided by $M^2$ tends to $\theta<0$, contradicting the nonnegative left-hand side.]
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Lemma 7
items.statement:
LEMMA 7. Let $(p_k)$ be a nonnegative sequence such that

$$
p _ {k} - \omega p _ {k - 1} \leq K
$$

for some $\omega < 1$ , some $K \in \mathbf{R}$ , and all sufficiently large $k$ . Then $(p_k)$ is bounded.
items.proof: Proof. If $\omega \leq 0$ the result is immediate. [Indeed, if $\omega\le0$ then $p_k\le K$ for all sufficiently large $k$, so nonnegativity bounds the tail.] If $\omega \in (0,1)$ , a simple induction argument shows that [Starting from the recurrence, repeatedly substitute the preceding bound; the finite geometric sum is $\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\omega^j=(1-\omega^k)/(1-\omega)$.] $p_k \leq \omega^k p_0 + K\sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \omega^j \leq p_0 + K(1-\omega)^{-1}$ and so $(p_k)$ is bounded.
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Opial's Lemma
items.statement: Let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in a Hilbert space and let $S\ne\emptyset$. If (a) for every $q\in S$, $\lim_n\|x_n-q\|$ exists, and (b) every weak sequential cluster point of $(x_n)$ belongs to $S$, then $(x_n)$ converges weakly to an element of $S$.
items.proof: Cited from: Z. Opial, “Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings,” *Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.* 73 (1967), 591–597.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Hilbert.WeakConvergence] recall opial_lemma

items.name: Boundedly inf-compact function
items.statement:
A function $f : H \to R \cup \{+\infty\}$ is boundedly inf-compact if for each $r \in R$ and R > 0 the set

$$
\Gamma_ {r} ^ {R} = \{v \in H: f (v) \leq r \text {and} \| v \| \leq R \}
$$

is relatively compact for the strong topology.
items.remark: [Note: relative compactness is for the strong topology]

items.name: Lemma 13
items.statement:
LEMMA 13. Let $(p_k)$ and $(\varepsilon_k)$ be real sequences such that $\limsup_{k\to +\infty}\varepsilon_k\leq 0$ and

$$
p _ {k + 1} \leq \eta p _ {k} + \varepsilon_ {k}
$$

for some $\eta \in (0,1)$ and all sufficiently large $k$ . Then $\limsup_{k\to +\infty}p_k\leq 0$ .
items.proof:
Proof. A simple induction argument shows that [For $k=1$ this is the recurrence. If it holds at $k$, multiply it by $\eta$ and add $\varepsilon_k$; this produces the formula at $k+1$.]

$$
p _ {k} \leq \eta^ {k} p _ {0} + \sum_ {j = 0} ^ {k - 1} \eta^ {k - j - 1} \varepsilon_ {j}.
$$

Set $C_k = \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} \varepsilon_j \eta^{k-j-1}$ . Since $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \eta^k p_0 = 0$ , it suffices to prove that $\limsup_{k \to +\infty} C_k \leq 0$ . To this end, fix $\varepsilon > 0$ . Since $\limsup_{k \to +\infty} \varepsilon_k \leq 0$ , there exists $k_\varepsilon > 0$ such that $\varepsilon_j \leq \varepsilon$ for all $j \geq k_\varepsilon$ . Then, for all $k > k_\varepsilon$ we have

$$
C _ {k} \leq \sum_ {j = 0} ^ {k _ {\varepsilon} - 1} \eta^ {k - j - 1} \varepsilon_ {j} + \sum_ {j = k _ {\varepsilon}} ^ {k} \eta^ {k - j - 1} \varepsilon_ {j} \leq \eta^ {k - 1} M _ {\varepsilon} + \frac {\varepsilon}{1 - \eta},
$$

where the quantity $M_{\varepsilon} = \sum_{j=0}^{k_{\varepsilon}-1} \eta^{-j} \varepsilon_j$ is independent of $k$ . Letting $k \to +\infty$ we deduce that

$$
\operatorname * {l i m s u p} _ {k \to + \infty} C _ {k} \leq \frac {\varepsilon}{1 - \eta}.
$$

This being true for any $\varepsilon > 0$ , the conclusion follows.

items.name: Convex subdifferential
items.statement: For a proper convex function $f:H\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ and $u\in H$, $$\partial f(u):=\{g\in H:\; f(v)\ge f(u)+\langle g,v-u\rangle\ \text{for every }v\in H\}.$$ Thus $g\in\partial f(u)$ is exactly the subdifferential inequality used below.
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Weak-to-weak sequential continuity
items.statement: A map $T:H\to H$ is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous if, for every sequence $(x_n)$ and $x\in H$, $$x_n\rightharpoonup x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad T(x_n)\rightharpoonup T(x).$$
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Topology.Sequences] use sequential weak-convergence API

items.name: Strong convexity
items.statement: A function $f:H\to\mathbf{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ is strongly convex with parameter $\rho>0$ if for every $x,y\in\operatorname{dom}f$ and $t\in[0,1]$, $$f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-\frac{\rho}{2}t(1-t)\|x-y\|^2.$$ Equivalently, when $g\in\partial f(x)$, $$f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2.$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Proximity operator
items.statement: For proper lower-semicontinuous convex $f$ and $x\in H$, $$\operatorname{prox}_f(x):=\underset{v\in H}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left(f(v)+\frac12\|v-x\|^2\right).$$ In particular, the paper writes $\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\Phi}$ for the proximity operator of $\lambda\Phi$.
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Metric projection onto a closed convex set
items.statement: For a nonempty closed convex set $C\subseteq H$, $$\operatorname{Proj}_C(x):=\underset{v\in C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\,\|v-x\|.$$ The minimizer is unique in a Hilbert space.
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Projection.BestApproximation] recall isChebyshev_of_nonempty_isClosed_convex

items.name: Indicator function of a set
items.statement: For $C\subseteq H$, its indicator function is $$\delta_C(x):=\begin{cases}0,&x\in C,\\+\infty,&x\notin C.\end{cases}$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Distance to a set
items.statement: For $C\subseteq H$ and $x\in H$, $$\operatorname{dist}(x,C):=\inf_{v\in C}\|x-v\|.$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Descent lemma for a Lipschitz gradient
items.statement: If $\Psi:H\to\mathbf{R}$ is differentiable and $\nabla\Psi$ is $L_\Psi$-Lipschitz, then for all $x,v\in H$, $$\Psi(v)\leq\Psi(x)+\langle\nabla\Psi(x),v-x\rangle+\frac{L_\Psi}{2}\|v-x\|^2.$$
items.proof: Cited from: D. Bertsekas, *Nonlinear Programming*, Proposition A.24 (1999); J. M. Ortega and W. C. Rheinboldt, *Iterative Solution of Nonlinear Equations in Several Variables* (2000).
items.remark: [Prove hint: apply the standard smoothness/descent inequality with $x=u_k$ and $v=u_{k+1}$]

items.name: Inertial forward-backward (IFB)
items.statement:
More precisely, start with $(u_{0}, y_{0}) \in H \times H$ . At the kth iteration, given $(u_{k}, y_{k})$ compute $u_{k+1}$ and then $y_{k+1}$ using the following rule:

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 0 \in \frac {u _ {k + 1} - u _ {k}}{\lambda} + \partial \Phi (u _ {k + 1}) + a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, \\ 0 = \frac {y _ {k + 1} - y _ {k}}{\lambda} + \nabla \Psi (u _ {k + 1}) - a u _ {k + 1} + b y _ {k + 1}, \end{array} \right. \tag {IFB}
$$

where a, b, and $\lambda$ are positive constants. (IFB stands for inertial forward-backward.) As we shall see, this algorithm keeps the physical interpretation of (1.4), which will allow us to find energy-type Liapunov functions.
items.remark: [Notation: $0\in\cdots+\partial\Phi(u)$ means an existential subgradient]

items.name: Parameter $\gamma$
items.statement:
$$
\gamma = \frac {1 - a \lambda}{2 b \lambda^ {2}} > 0, \tag {3.1}
$$

where the inequality follows from $H_{\lambda}$ .

items.name: Gradient-projection algorithm
items.statement:
$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} u _ {k + 1} = \operatorname{Proj} _ {C} \left(\lambda y _ {k} + (1 - \lambda) u _ {k}\right), \\ y _ {k + 1} = (1 - \mu) y _ {k} + \mu \left(u _ {k + 1} - \nabla \Psi (u _ {k + 1})\right), \end{array} \right. \tag {5.1}
$$

where $\mu = \frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda}$ , and will be referred to as the gradient-projection algorithm. Figure 5.1 illustrates how the two subiterations are performed. items.name: Classical gradient-projection algorithm
items.statement:
The classical forward-backward splitting algorithm (gradient-projection) reads as follows. Take $u_{0} \in R^{n}$ and $0 < \lambda < 2$ . For $k = 0, 1, \ldots$ ,

$$
u _ {k + 1} = \mathrm{Proj} _ {C} \left((1 - \lambda) u _ {k} + \lambda \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {p} \omega_ {i} \mathrm{Proj} _ {C _ {i}} (u _ {k})\right). \tag {5.4}
$$
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Projection.BestApproximation] recall projection theorem

items.name: Inertial CQ algorithm
items.statement:
The classical forward-backward algorithm when applied to this structured minimization problem gives rise to the so-called CQ algorithm, originally introduced by Byrne in [20]:

$$
u _ {k + 1} = \mathrm{Proj} _ {C} \left(u _ {k} - \lambda A ^ {t} (I - \mathrm{Proj} _ {Q}) A u _ {k}\right). \tag {5.13}
$$
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Projection.BestApproximation] recall projection theorem

items.name: Iterative shrinkage/thresholding algorithm (ISTA)
items.statement:
The classical forward-backward operator provides the so-called iterative shrinkage/thresholding algorithm (ISTA) (see [15, 16])

$$
u _ {k + 1} = \mathrm{prox} _ {\lambda \gamma \| \cdot \| _ {1}} \left(u _ {k} - 2 \lambda A ^ {t} (A u _ {k} - b)\right). \tag {5.18}
$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Auxiliary sequence $G_k(q)$
items.statement:
Given $q \in H$ and $k \geq 2$ , we define the auxiliary sequence $(G_{k}(q))$ by

$$
G _ {k} (q) = \langle z _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle - \sum_ {i = 2} ^ {k} \langle z _ {i}, \xi_ {i} \rangle , \tag {3.11}
$$

where $z_{k}$ is given by (3.4).
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Proposition 12
items.statement:
PROPOSITION 12. Let $(u_k, y_k)$ satisfy (IFB). The following holds:

(i) If $(u_k)$ converges weakly to some $u_{\infty}$ and $\nabla \Psi$ is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous, then $(y_k)$ converges weakly to some $y_{\infty}$ ;  
(ii) If $(u_k)$ converges strongly to some $u_{\infty}$ , then $(y_k)$ converges strongly to some $y_{\infty}$ .

In either case, we have

$$
\nabla \Psi (u _ {\infty}) - a u _ {\infty} + b y _ {\infty} = 0. \tag {4.3}
$$
items.proof:
Proof of Proposition 12. For $k \geq 1$ , set

(4.4) $bw_{k}=au_{k+1}-\nabla\Psi(u_{k+1}).$

Let $u_{\infty}$ be the (weak or strong) limit of the sequence $(u_k)$ as $k \to +\infty$ and set

$$
b y _ {\infty} = a u _ {\infty} - \nabla \Psi (u _ {\infty})
$$

so that (4.2) can be rewritten as

(4.5) $(y_{k+1}-y_{\infty})=\eta(y_{k}-y_{\infty})+\lambda b\eta(w_{k}-y_{\infty}),$

where $\eta = \frac{1}{1 + \lambda b} \in (0,1)$ .

In order to prove (i), let $(u_{k})$ converge weakly to $u_{\infty}$ as $k\to +\infty$ . Since $\nabla \Psi$ is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous, the sequence $(w_{k})$ converges weakly to $y_{\infty}$ as $k\rightarrow +\infty$ . Take $\xi \in H$ and multiply (4.5) by $\xi$ to obtain

$$
\langle y _ {k + 1} - y _ {\infty}, \xi \rangle = \eta \langle y _ {k} - y _ {\infty}, \xi \rangle + \lambda b \eta \langle w _ {k} - y _ {\infty}, \xi \rangle .
$$

Use Lemma 13 with $p_k = \langle y_k - y_\infty, \xi \rangle$ and $\varepsilon_k = \lambda b\eta \langle w_k - y_\infty, \xi \rangle$ to deduce that

$$
\operatorname * {l i m s u p} _ {k \to + \infty} \langle y _ {k} - y _ {\infty}, \xi \rangle \leq 0
$$

for all $\xi \in H$ . Replacing $\xi$ by $-\xi$ we conclude that

$$
\operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {k \to + \infty} \langle y _ {k} - y _ {\infty}, \xi \rangle \geq 0
$$

and so $(y_{k})$ converges weakly to $y_{\infty}$ . [For each $\xi$, the limsup bound for $\xi$ and the corresponding bound for $-\xi$ give liminf $\ge0$; hence the scalar products converge to $0$, which is the definition of weak convergence.]

To prove (ii), use (4.5) and the triangle inequality to deduce that

$$
\| y _ {k + 1} - y _ {\infty} \| \leq \eta \| y _ {k} - y _ {\infty} \| + \lambda b \eta \| w _ {k} - y _ {\infty} \|.
$$

Recall that $\lim_{k\to+\infty}\|w_k-y_\infty\|=0$ if $(u_k)$ converges strongly to $u_\infty$ as $k\to+\infty$ , and use Lemma 13 with $p_k=\|y_k-y_\infty\|$ and $\varepsilon_k=\lambda b\eta\|w_k-y_\infty\|$ to conclude that $\lim_{k\to+\infty}\|y_k-y_\infty\|=0$ . [Lemma 13 gives $\limsup p_k\le0$; since $p_k=\|y_k-y_\infty\|\ge0$, this is equivalent to $p_k\to0$.] ☐
items.remark: [Prove hint: scalarize weak convergence against arbitrary $\xi$, then use Lemma 13 for both $\xi$ and $-\xi$]

items.name: General IFB gradient-projection algorithm
items.statement:
(iii) Take now general positive parameters $a$ and $b$ . The (IFB) algorithm reads

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} u _ {k + 1} = \operatorname{Proj} _ {C} \left((1 - \lambda a) u _ {k} + \lambda b y _ {k}\right), \\ y _ {k + 1} = \frac {1}{1 + \lambda b} y _ {k} + \frac {\lambda a}{1 + \lambda b} u _ {k + 1} - \frac {\lambda}{1 + \lambda b} \left(u _ {k + 1} - \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {p} \omega_ {i} \operatorname{Proj} _ {C _ {i}} (u _ {k + 1})\right). \end{array} \right. \tag {5.6}
$$
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Projection.BestApproximation] recall projection theorem

items.name: IFB CQ algorithm
items.statement:
Let us now consider the (IFB) algorithm and apply it to the structured minimization problem (5.12):

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} u _ {k + 1} = \operatorname{Proj} _ {C} \left((1 - \lambda a) u _ {k} + \lambda b y _ {k}\right), \\ y _ {k + 1} = \frac {1}{1 + \lambda b} y _ {k} + \frac {\lambda a}{1 + \lambda b} u _ {k + 1} - \frac {\lambda}{1 + \lambda b} \left(u _ {k + 1} - A ^ {t} (I - \operatorname{Proj} _ {Q}) A (u _ {k + 1})\right). \end{array} \right. \tag {5.14}
$$
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Projection.BestApproximation] recall projection theorem

items.name: IFB signal-recovery algorithm
items.statement:
Let us now consider the (IFB) algorithm and apply it to the structured minimization problem $(5.15)$ :

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} u _ {k + 1} = \operatorname{prox} _ {\lambda \gamma \| \cdot \| _ {1}} \left((1 - \lambda a) u _ {k} + \lambda b y _ {k}\right), \\ y _ {k + 1} = \frac {1}{1 + \lambda b} y _ {k} + \frac {\lambda a}{1 + \lambda b} u _ {k + 1} - \frac {2 \lambda}{1 + \lambda b} A ^ {t} (A u _ {k + 1} - b). \end{array} \right. \tag {5.19}
$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Proposition 2
items.statement: PROPOSITION 2. Let Hypothesis $H$ hold. $^{1}$ Then the sequence $(E_k)$ is non-increasing and $\lim_{k \to +\infty} E_k$ exists. Moreover, $(\|\xi_k\|) \in \ell^2$ and $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \Theta(u_k) = \lim_{k \to +\infty} E_k$ .
items.proof:
Proof. Since $\Theta$ is bounded from below, so is $(E_k)$ . Therefore, it suffices to prove that there exists $\beta > 0$ such that $E_{k+1} - E_k + \beta \| \xi_{k+1} \|^2 \leq 0$ for every $k \geq 1$ . [Indeed, summing this inequality from a fixed index to $N$ makes $(E_k)$ decreasing and yields $\beta\sum_{k}\|\xi_{k+1}\|^2\le E_1-\inf\Theta$; hence the asserted limit and $\ell^2$ summability follow.]

First, let us write the subdifferential inequality for $\Phi$ at point $u_{k + 1}$ ; for all $v\in H$ , we have

$$
\Phi (v) \geq \Phi (u _ {k + 1}) + \left\langle \frac {u _ {k + 1} - u _ {k}}{\lambda} + a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k + 1} - v \right\rangle .
$$

Setting $v = u_{k}$ , we deduce that

$$
\Phi (u _ {k}) \geq \Phi (u _ {k + 1}) + \left\langle \frac {u _ {k + 1} - u _ {k}}{\lambda} + a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k + 1} - u _ {k} \right\rangle ,
$$

and so

$$
\Phi (u _ {k + 1}) - \Phi (u _ {k}) + \frac {1}{\lambda} \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} + \langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \leq 0. \tag {3.5}
$$

On the other hand, the descent lemma for $\Psi$ [17, Proposition A.24], [33] gives [The hypotheses of this result are exactly $H_\Psi$: differentiability and $L_\Psi$-Lipschitz continuity of $\nabla\Psi$.]

$$
\Psi (v) \leq \Psi (u _ {k}) + \langle \nabla \Psi (u _ {k}), v - u _ {k} \rangle + \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} \| v - u _ {k} \| ^ {2},
$$

which, in view of the second (IFB) equation, yields

$$
\Psi (v) \leq \Psi (u _ {k}) + \left\langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k} - \frac {y _ {k} - y _ {k - 1}}{\lambda}, v - u _ {k} \right\rangle + \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} \| v - u _ {k} \| ^ {2}.
$$

Setting $v = u_{k + 1}$ , we obtain

$$
\Psi (u _ {k + 1}) - \Psi (u _ {k}) - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} - \langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \leq - \frac {1}{\lambda} \langle \zeta_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle , \tag {3.6}
$$

where $\zeta_{k}$ is defined in (3.3). Adding inequalities (3.5) and (3.6) we obtain

$$
\Theta (u _ {k + 1}) - \Theta (u _ {k}) + \left[ \frac {1}{\lambda} - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} \right] \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \leq - \frac {1}{\lambda} \langle \zeta_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle . \tag {3.7}
$$

Recall from (3.4) that $z_{k+1} = \frac{\xi_{k+1}}{\lambda} + au_k - by_k \in -\partial \Phi(u_{k+1})$ . We use the monotonicity of $\partial \Phi$ at points $u_k$ and $u_{k+1}$ to deduce that

$$
\left\langle \frac {\xi_ {k + 1}}{\lambda} + a u _ {k} - b y _ {k} - \frac {\xi_ {k}}{\lambda} - a u _ {k - 1} + b y _ {k - 1}, u _ {k + 1} - u _ {k} \right\rangle \leq 0.
$$

We can rewrite this as

$$
\frac {1}{\lambda} \langle \xi_ {k + 1} - \xi_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle + a \langle \xi_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle - b \langle \zeta_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \leq 0.
$$

Dividing by $b\lambda$ and rearranging the terms we obtain, with $\gamma$ defined by (3.1), [Here the coefficient of $\langle\xi_k,\xi_{k+1}\rangle$ is $(1-a\lambda)/(b\lambda^2)=2\gamma$, so moving all terms to the displayed side gives (3.8).]

$$
- \frac {1}{\lambda} \langle \zeta_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle + \frac {1}{b \lambda^ {2}} \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} - 2 \gamma \langle \xi_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \leq 0. \tag {3.8}
$$

Since

$$
2 \langle \xi_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \leq \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} + \| \xi_ {k} \| ^ {2},
$$

inequality (3.8) gives

$$
- \frac {1}{\lambda} \langle \zeta_ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle + \left[ \frac {1}{b \lambda^ {2}} - \gamma \right] \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} - \gamma \| \xi_ {k} \| ^ {2} \leq 0. \tag {3.9}
$$

Adding inequalities (3.7) and (3.9) we see that

$$
\Theta (u _ {k + 1}) - \Theta (u _ {k}) + \left[ \frac {1}{\lambda} - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} + \frac {1}{b \lambda^ {2}} - \gamma \right] \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} - \gamma \| \xi_ {k} \| ^ {2} \leq 0
$$

and recalling the definition of $E_{k}$ we deduce that

$$
E _ {k + 1} - E _ {k} + \left[ \frac {1}{\lambda} - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} + \frac {1}{b \lambda^ {2}} - 2 \gamma \right] \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \leq 0.
$$

Having $H_{\lambda}$ in mind, it suffices to set

$$
\beta = \frac {1}{\lambda} - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} + \frac {1}{b \lambda^ {2}} - 2 \gamma = \frac {2 (a + b) - b \lambda L _ {\Psi}}{2 b \lambda} > 0 \tag {3.10}
$$

to complete the proof. [The preceding summation argument also gives $\xi_k\to0$; since $E_k-\Theta(u_k)=\gamma\|\xi_k\|^2$, the two limits coincide.] □
items.remark: [Prove hint: add the subgradient and descent inequalities, then telescope the energy estimate]

items.name: Liapunov-type sequence $F_k(q)$
items.statement:
Next, we define the sequence $(F_{k}(q))$ , by

$$
F _ {k} (q) = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) G _ {k + 1} (q) - \delta \sum_ {i = 2} ^ {k} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} + 2 \alpha \langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \tag {3.12}
$$

with

$$
\alpha = \frac {1 + b \lambda}{2 \lambda^ {2}} \quad \text {and} \quad \delta = \frac {2 + (b - a) \lambda}{2 \lambda^ {2}}.
$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Sequence $A_k(q)$
items.statement:
For $q\in H$ define

$$
A _ {k} (q) = \left(\frac {a + b}{2 \lambda}\right) \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) G _ {k + 1} (q) \tag {3.23}
$$
items.remark: [Notation: preserve the paper\x27s sequence indexing and make all ambient-space hypotheses explicit in Lean.]

items.name: Proposition 3
items.statement:
PROPOSITION 3. Assume $\Theta$ is convex. For each $q\in H$ and $k\geq 1$ we have

(3.13)

$$
b (\Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {k + 1})) \geq b \left\langle \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} - a\right) \xi_ {k + 1} + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle = F _ {k + 1} (q) - F _ {k} (q).
$$

In particular, the sequence $(F_k(q))$ is nonincreasing whenever $q \in S$ .
items.proof:
Proof. First observe that since $\Theta$ is convex and

$$
0 \in \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} - a\right) \xi_ {k} + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \zeta_ {k} + \partial \Theta (u _ {k}), \tag {3.14}
$$

we must have

$$
\left\langle \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} - a\right) \xi_ {k} + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \zeta_ {k}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle \leq \Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {k}),
$$

which proves the inequality. [Indeed, (3.14) says the negative of the displayed vector lies in $\partial\Theta(u_k)$, and the subdifferential inequality with $v=q$ gives precisely the claimed bound.] Let us now prove that the product above can be written as the difference of consecutive terms of the sequence $(F_{k}(q))$ . From the definition of $G_{k}(q)$ given in (3.11) we have

$$
G _ {k + 2} (q) - G _ {k + 1} (q) = \langle z _ {k + 2}, u _ {k + 2} - q \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 2}, \xi_ {k + 2} \rangle .
$$

We deduce that

$$
\begin{array}{l} F _ {k + 1} (q) - F _ {k} (q) \tag {3.15} \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 2}, \xi_ {k + 2} \rangle - \delta \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle z _ {k + 2}, u _ {k + 2} - q \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle \right] \\ + 2 \alpha \left[ \left\langle \xi_ {k + 2}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle \right] \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 2}, \xi_ {k + 2} \rangle - \delta \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ \left. - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle z _ {k + 2}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 1}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right] \right. \\ + 2 \alpha \left[ \langle \xi_ {k + 2}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right] \\ - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle z _ {k + 2}, \xi_ {k + 2} \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \right] \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle - \delta \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ \left. - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle z _ {k + 2} - \frac {\xi_ {k + 2}}{\lambda}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle z _ {k + 1} - \frac {\xi_ {k + 1}}{\lambda}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right] \right. \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle - \delta \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ \left. - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right]. \right. \\ \end{array}
$$

Keeping this in mind, let us rewrite the quantity

$$
B _ {k + 1} (q) = b \left\langle \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} - a\right) \xi_ {k + 1} + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle
$$

on the right-hand side of the equality in (3.13). First observe that

(3.16)

$$
\begin{array}{l} B _ {k + 1} (q) \\ = \frac {b}{\lambda} \left\langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - b \left\langle a \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left\langle b \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle \\ = \frac {a + b}{\lambda} \left\langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left\langle a \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left\langle b \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle \\ = \frac {a + b}{\lambda} \left\langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left\langle a \xi_ {k + 1} - b \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} + \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \right] - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle a \xi_ {k + 1} - b \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle . \\ \end{array}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{array}{l} \langle a \xi_ {k + 1} - b \zeta_ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle \\ = \left\langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \right\rangle \\ = \left\langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle + \frac {1}{\lambda} \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ - \left\langle \frac {\xi_ {k + 1}}{\lambda} + a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, \xi_ {k + 1} \right\rangle \\ = \left\langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle \\ + \frac {1}{\lambda} \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} - \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle . \\ \end{array}
$$

Using this in (3.16) we deduce that

$$
\begin{array}{l} = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left[ \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} - \frac {1}{\lambda} \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \right] \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ \left. - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right] \right. \\ + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle \\ = \frac {a + b}{2 \lambda} \left[ \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \right] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {k + 1}, \xi_ {k + 1} \rangle - \delta \| \xi_ {k + 1} \| ^ {2} \\ \left. - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \langle a u _ {k + 1} - b y _ {k + 1}, u _ {k + 1} - q \rangle - \langle a u _ {k} - b y _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \right]. \right. \\ \end{array}
$$

(3.17) $B_{k + 1}(q)$

The right-hand sides of (3.15) and (3.17) coincide, and the equality in (3.13) is verified. ☐
items.remark: [Prove hint: derive (3.14) by adding IFB equations and use the convex subgradient inequality]

items.name: Proposition 4
items.statement: PROPOSITION 4. Let hypotheses $H_{\Phi}$ and $H_{\Psi}$ hold. Then, for each $q \in \text{dom}(\Phi)$ , the sequence $(G_k(q))$ is bounded from above.
items.proof:
Proof. First write

$$
G _ {k} (q) = \langle z _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle - \sum_ {i = 2} ^ {k} \langle z _ {i - 1}, u _ {i} - u _ {i - 1} \rangle - \sum_ {i = 2} ^ {k} \langle z _ {i} - z _ {i - 1}, \xi_ {i} \rangle . \tag {3.18}
$$

The subdifferential inequality for $\Phi$ gives

$$
\langle z _ {k}, u _ {k} - q \rangle \leq \Phi (q) - \Phi (u _ {k}) \tag {3.19}
$$

and

$$
- \langle z _ {i - 1}, u _ {i} - u _ {i - 1} \rangle \leq \Phi (u _ {i}) - \Phi (u _ {i - 1}) \tag {3.20}
$$

because $-z_{j} \in \partial \Phi(u_{j})$ for each j. On the other hand,

$$
\begin{array}{l} - \langle z _ {i} - z _ {i - 1}, \xi_ {i} \rangle = - \left\langle \frac {\xi_ {i} - \xi_ {i - 1}}{\lambda} + a \xi_ {i - 1} - b \zeta_ {i - 1}, \xi_ {i} \right\rangle \tag {3.21} \\ = - \frac {1}{\lambda} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} + \frac {1 - a \lambda}{\lambda} \langle \xi_ {i - 1}, \xi_ {i} \rangle + b \langle \zeta_ {i - 1}, \xi_ {i} \rangle \\ \leq - \frac {1}{\lambda} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} + \frac {1 - a \lambda}{2 \lambda} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} + \frac {1 - a \lambda}{2 \lambda} \| \xi_ {i - 1} \| ^ {2} \\ + b \lambda (\Theta (u _ {i - 1}) - \Theta (u _ {i})) - b \lambda \left[ \frac {1}{\lambda} - \frac {L _ {\Psi}}{2} \right] \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} \\ \leq \left[ \frac {b \lambda^ {2} L _ {\Psi} - (a + 2 b) \lambda - 1}{2 \lambda} \right] \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} \\ + \frac {1 - a \lambda}{2 \lambda} \| \xi_ {i - 1} \| ^ {2} + b \lambda (\Theta (u _ {i - 1}) - \Theta (u _ {i})) \\ \end{array}
$$

by inequality (3.7). Using inequalities (3.19), (3.20), and (3.21) in equality (3.18) we deduce that

$$
G _ {k} (q) \leq \Phi (q) - \Phi (u _ {1}) + b \lambda (\Theta (u _ {1}) - \Theta (u _ {k})) + K \sum_ {i = 1} ^ {k} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2}
$$

for some positive constant K. [More explicitly, summing (3.20) telescopes the $\Phi$-increments, and the two $\Theta$-increments in (3.21) telescope; the remaining squared-velocity sums are finite by Proposition 2.] The right-hand side is finite by virtue of Proposition 2. ☐
items.remark: [Prove hint: telescope (3.18) after applying the subgradient inequalities]

items.name: Proposition 6
items.statement: PROPOSITION 6. Assume hypothesis H holds. Then $\lim_{k\to+\infty}\Theta(u_k)=\inf\Theta$ . In particular, every weak cluster point of the sequence $(u_k)$ lies in S. As a consequence, if $S=\emptyset$ , then $\lim_{k\to+\infty}\|u_k\|=+\infty$ .
items.proof:
Proof. From Proposition 3 and the definition of $E_{k}$ we deduce that for each $q \in H$ ,

$$
F _ {k} (q) - F _ {k - 1} (q) \leq b (\Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {k})) = b (\Theta (q) - E _ {k}) + b \gamma \| \xi_ {k} \| ^ {2}.
$$

Let $E_{\infty} = \lim_{k\to +\infty}E_k = \lim_{k\to +\infty}\Theta (u_k)$ . Since the sequence $(E_k)$ is nonincreasing we have

$$
F _ {k} (q) - F _ {k - 1} (q) \leq b (\Theta (q) - E _ {\infty}) + b \gamma \| \xi_ {k} \| ^ {2}.
$$

On the other hand, inequality (3.22) shows that

$$
\alpha \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} - \alpha \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \leq F _ {k} (q) - C
$$

for some constant $C$ . Taking $a_{k} = F_{k}(q) - C$ , $b_{k} = \alpha \| u_{k} - q\|^{2}$ , $\varepsilon_{k} = b\gamma \| \xi_{k}\|^{2}$ (which is in $\ell^1$ by Proposition 2), and $\theta = b(\Theta (q) - E_{\infty})$ in Lemma 5, we deduce that $E_{\infty}\leq \Theta (q)$ . Since this holds for any $q\in H$ we have $E_{\infty} = \inf \Theta$ .

Observe that the sequence $(u_k)$ is minimizing even if $S = \emptyset$ .
items.remark: [Foundation: Foundation.Topology.Sequences] use weak cluster-point API; prove minimizing-sequence conclusion before lower semicontinuity]

items.name: Proposition 8
items.statement: PROPOSITION 8. Assume hypothesis $H$ holds and let $\mathcal{S} \neq \emptyset$ . Then the sequence $(u_k)$ is bounded. Moreover, $\lim_{k \to +\infty} F_k(q)$ exists for each $q \in \mathcal{S}$ .
items.proof:
Proof. Take $q \in S$ . By Proposition 3, the sequence $(F_k(q))$ is nonincreasing. Inequality (3.22) then gives

$$
\| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} - \left[ \frac {2 \alpha \lambda - a - b}{2 \alpha \lambda} \right] \| u _ {k - 1} - q \| ^ {2} \leq \left[ \frac {F _ {1} (q) - C}{\alpha} \right].
$$

Since $\frac{2\alpha\lambda-a-b}{2\alpha\lambda}\in(0,1)$ , Lemma 7 shows that the sequence $(\|u_{k}-q\|)$ is bounded. [Apply Lemma 7 to $p_k=\|u_k-q\|^2$, with the displayed coefficient as $\omega$ and the displayed constant as $K$.] Using inequality (3.22) again we deduce that the sequence $(F_{k}(q))$ is bounded from below. Since it is nonincreasing, it must converge. ☐
items.remark: [Prove hint: apply Lemma 7 to the recurrence obtained from (3.22)]

items.name: Theorem 1
items.statement:
THEOREM 1. Let Hypothesis H hold. Then $\lim_{k\to+\infty}\Theta(u_k)=\inf\Theta$ . Assume moreover that S=Argmin $\Theta\neq\emptyset$ and any of the following conditions holds:

(i) The set $\mathcal{S}$ is a singleton.  
(ii) The function $\Phi$ is differentiable and its gradient is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous.  
(iii) The gradient of $\Psi$ is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous.  
(iv) The function $\Psi$ is convex.

Then any sequence $(u_{k})$ generated by algorithm (IFB) converges weakly as $k \to +\infty$ to an element of S. On the other hand, if $S = \emptyset$ , then $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \|u_{k}\| = +\infty$ .
items.proof:
The final statement follows directly from Proposition 6. [Proposition 6 proves that $(u_k)$ is minimizing; if it did not escape every norm ball when $\mathcal S=\emptyset$, a bounded subsequence would admit a weak cluster point, which Proposition 6 would place in $\mathcal S$, a contradiction.] Let us assume that $S \neq \emptyset$ and prove the weak convergence of $(u_k)$ to an element of S. We shall analyze each case separately.

Case (i). It is immediate from Propositions 6 and 8. [Proposition 8 gives boundedness, so weak cluster points exist; Proposition 6 puts each in the singleton $\mathcal S$, hence all cluster points coincide and the bounded sequence converges weakly to that point.]

For cases (ii) and (iii) we shall prove that the sequence $(u_{k})$ can have at most one weak cluster point. But before doing so, let us turn our attention to the first two terms in the definition of $F_{k}(q)$ . For $q\in H$ define

$$
A _ {k} (q) = \left(\frac {a + b}{2 \lambda}\right) \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) G _ {k + 1} (q) \tag {3.23}
$$

and observe that $\lim_{k\to +\infty}A_k(q)$ exists whenever $q\in \mathcal{S}$ . Indeed, recall from (3.12) that

$$
F _ {k} (q) = A _ {k} (q) - \delta \sum_ {i = 2} ^ {k} \| \xi_ {i} \| ^ {2} + 2 \alpha \langle \xi_ {k + 1}, u _ {k} - q \rangle .
$$

We know that $(\|\xi_{i}\|)$ belongs to $\ell^{2}$ by Proposition 2 and that $(u_{k})$ is bounded by Proposition 8; hence $\lim_{k\to+\infty}F_{k}(q)-A_{k}(q)$ exists. But $\lim_{k\to+\infty}F_{k}(q)$ also exists since $q\in S$ (also by Proposition 8).

Now take $p, q \in H$ and $m, n \in N$ . We have

$$
\begin{array}{l} A _ {m} (p) - A _ {n} (p) - A _ {m} (q) + A _ {n} (q) \tag {3.24} \\ = \left(\frac {a + b}{\lambda}\right) \langle u _ {m} - u _ {n}, q - p \rangle - \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \langle z _ {m + 1} - z _ {n + 1}, q - p \rangle . \\ \end{array}
$$

Assume $u_{t_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{p}$ and $u_{s_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{q}$ as $k \to +\infty$ . By Proposition 6, both $\bar{p}$ and $\bar{q}$ must be in $S$ . Observe also that since $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \xi_k = 0$ we have $u_{t_k - 1} \rightharpoonup \bar{p}$ and $u_{s_k - 1} \rightharpoonup \bar{q}$ as $k \to +\infty$ . Use $p = \bar{p}$ , $q = \bar{q}$ , $m = t_k - 1$ , and $n = s_k - 1$ in (3.24). Then let $k \to +\infty$ to obtain

$$
\lim _ {k \to + \infty} \langle z _ {t _ {k}} - z _ {s _ {k}}, \bar {p} - \bar {q} \rangle = \left(\frac {a + b}{1 + b \lambda}\right) \| \bar {p} - \bar {q} \| ^ {2}. \tag {3.25}
$$

This fact will be used in what follows.

Case (ii). Since $\nabla \Phi$ is weak-to-weak sequentially continuous, if $u_{t_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{p}$ and $u_{s_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{q}$ as $k \to +\infty$ , we deduce that

$$
\lim _ {k \to + \infty} \langle z _ {t _ {k}} - z _ {s _ {k}}, \bar {p} - \bar {q} \rangle = - \langle \nabla \Phi (\bar {p}) - \nabla \Phi (\bar {q}), \bar {p} - \bar {q} \rangle \leq 0
$$

by the monotonicity of $\nabla \Phi$ . Then (3.25) implies that $\bar{p} = \bar{q}$ .

Case (iii). Observe that $\left(\frac{1}{\lambda} - a\right)\xi_k + \left(\frac{1}{\lambda} + b\right)\zeta_k = z_k - \nabla\Psi(u_k)$ . Proposition 3 implies

$$
F _ {k} (\bar {q}) - F _ {k - 1} (\bar {q}) = b \langle z _ {k} - \nabla \Psi (u _ {k}), u _ {k} - \bar {q} \rangle \tag {3.26}
$$

and this quantity vanishes as $k \to +\infty$ whenever $\bar{q} \in \mathcal{S}$ . For $q \in H$ set $\mathcal{A}_k(q) = \langle z_k - \nabla \Psi(u_k), u_k - q \rangle$ . A simple computation shows that for $p, q \in H$ and for $m, n \in \mathbf{N}$ we have [Expand each $\mathcal A_j(r)=\langle z_j-\nabla\Psi(u_j),u_j-r\rangle$; the $z_j$ terms combine into $\langle z_m-z_n,p-q\rangle$, and moving the gradient terms to the other side gives the displayed identity.]

$$
\langle \nabla \Psi (u _ {m}) - \nabla \Psi (u _ {n}), p - q \rangle = \mathcal {A} _ {m} (p) - \mathcal {A} _ {n} (p) - \mathcal {A} _ {m} (q) + \mathcal {A} _ {n} (q) + \langle z _ {m} - z _ {n}, p - q \rangle .
$$

If $u_{t_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{p}$ and $u_{s_k} \rightharpoonup \bar{q}$ as $k \to +\infty$ , then $\bar{p}, \bar{q} \in S$ and the previous equation gives

$$
\lim _ {k \to \infty} \left\langle \nabla \Psi (u _ {t _ {k}}) - \nabla \Psi (u _ {s _ {k}}), \bar {p} - \bar {q} \right\rangle = \lim _ {k \to \infty} \left\langle z _ {t _ {k}} - z _ {s _ {k}}, \bar {p} - \bar {q} \right\rangle .
$$

Thus, in view of (3.25) and the weak-to-weak sequential continuity of $\nabla \Psi$ , we conclude that

$$
\left(\frac {a + b}{1 + b \lambda}\right) \| \bar {p} - \bar {q} \| ^ {2} = \langle \nabla \Psi (\bar {p}) - \nabla \Psi (\bar {q}), \bar {p} - \bar {q} \rangle \leq 0
$$

because $\nabla\Psi(q)\in-\partial\Phi(q)$ whenever $q\in S$ . It ensues, as before, that $\bar{p}=\bar{q}$ .

Case (iv). Let $q \in S$ and $m > n$ . We have

$$
G _ {n + 1} (q) - G _ {m + 1} (q) = \left[ \langle z _ {n + 1}, u _ {n + 1} - q \rangle + \sum_ {i = n + 2} ^ {m + 1} \langle z _ {i}, \xi_ {i} \rangle \right] + \langle - z _ {m + 1}, u _ {m + 1} - q \rangle .
$$

On the one hand,

$$
\begin{array}{l} \langle z _ {n + 1}, u _ {n + 1} - q \rangle + \sum_ {i = n + 2} ^ {m + 1} \langle z _ {i}, \xi_ {i} \rangle \leq \Phi (q) - \Phi (u _ {n + 1}) + \sum_ {i = n + 2} ^ {m + 1} [ \Phi (u _ {i - 1}) - \Phi (u _ {i}) ] \\ = \Phi (q) - \Phi (u _ {m + 1}) \\ \end{array}
$$

by the convexity of $\Phi$ . On the other hand, equality (3.26) and the convexity of $\Psi$ imply

$$
\begin{array}{l} \left\langle - z _ {m + 1}, u _ {m + 1} - q \right\rangle = \left\langle - z _ {m + 1} + \nabla \Psi (u _ {m + 1}), u _ {m + 1} - q \right\rangle - \left\langle \nabla \Psi (u _ {m + 1}), u _ {m + 1} - q \right\rangle \\ \leq \frac {1}{b} [ F _ {m} (q) - F _ {m + 1} (q) ] + \Psi (q) - \Psi (u _ {m + 1}). \\ \end{array}
$$

From the above relations and the definition of $G$ , it follows that

$$
G _ {n + 1} (q) - G _ {m + 1} (q) \leq \Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {m + 1}) + \frac {1}{b} [ F _ {m} (q) - F _ {m + 1} (q) ].
$$

Thus, in view of (3.23),

$$
\begin{array}{l} \left(\frac {a + b}{2 \lambda}\right) \| u _ {n} - q \| ^ {2} \\ = \left(\frac {a + b}{2 \lambda}\right) \| u _ {m} - q \| ^ {2} + [ A _ {n} (q) - A _ {m} (q) ] + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) [ G _ {n + 1} (q) - G _ {m + 1} (q) ] \\ \leq \left(\frac {a + b}{2 \lambda}\right) \| u _ {m} - q \| ^ {2} + [ A _ {n} (q) - A _ {m} (q) ] \\ + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \left[ \frac {1}{b} [ F _ {m} (q) - F _ {m + 1} (q) ] + \Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {m + 1}) \right]. \\ \end{array}
$$

Take the lower limit as $m \to +\infty$ and recall that $\lim_{m \to +\infty} \Theta(u_m) = \Theta(q)$ . Then take the upper limit as $n \to +\infty$ to conclude that

$$
\operatorname * {l i m s u p} _ {n \to + \infty} \| u _ {n} - q \| \leq \operatorname * {l i m i n f} _ {m \to + \infty} \| u _ {m} - q \|.
$$

Therefore $\lim_{k\to +\infty}\| u_k - q\|$ exists and the result follows from Proposition 6 and Opial's lemma. [For every $q\in\mathcal S$ the preceding limsup/liminf inequality yields existence of $\lim_k\|u_k-q\|$; Proposition 6 says that every weak cluster point lies in $\mathcal S$. These are exactly the two hypotheses of Opial's lemma.]

items.name: Corollary 10
items.statement: COROLLARY 10. Assume hypothesis $H$ holds and let $\Theta$ be strongly convex. Then $(u_k)$ converges strongly to the unique $\bar{q} \in \mathcal{S}$ .
items.proof:
Assume $\Theta$ is strongly convex with parameter $\rho$ . In view of (3.14), for each $q \in H$ and $k \geq 1$ we have

$$
\left\langle \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} - a\right) \xi_ {k} + \left(\frac {1}{\lambda} + b\right) \zeta_ {k}, u _ {k} - q \right\rangle + \frac {\rho}{2} \| u _ {k} - q \| ^ {2} \leq \Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {k}),
$$

and so

$$
F _ {k + 1} (q) - F _ {k} (q) + \frac {\rho b}{2} \| u _ {k + 1} - q \| ^ {2} \leq b (\Theta (q) - \Theta (u _ {k + 1})) \tag {4.1}
$$

by the equality in (3.13). Moreover, since $\Theta$ is strongly convex, we have $S = \{\bar{q}\}$ . If Hypothesis $H$ holds, we can write $q = \bar{q}$ in inequality (4.1), let $k \to +\infty$ , and apply Propositions 6 and 8 to deduce that $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \|u_k - \bar{q}\| = 0$ . [Indeed, $F_k(\bar q)$ converges by Proposition 8, while the right-hand side of (4.1) tends to $0$ by Proposition 6; taking limits forces the nonnegative term $(\rho b/2)\|u_{k+1}-\bar q\|^2$ to vanish.] We have proved the following corollary.

COROLLARY 10. Assume hypothesis $H$ holds and let $\Theta$ be strongly convex. Then $(u_k)$ converges strongly to the unique $\bar{q} \in \mathcal{S}$ .
items.remark: [Prove hint: use the strong subgradient inequality and the limiting energy identity]

items.name: Corollary 11
items.statement: COROLLARY 11. Assume hypothesis $H$ holds and let $\Theta$ be boundedly inf-compact. If $(u_k)$ converges weakly as $k \to +\infty$ , then it converges strongly and the limit belongs to $S$ .
items.proof: Proof. If $(u_{k})$ converges weakly as $k \to +\infty$ , then it is bounded. By Proposition 6, the weak limit belongs to $S \neq \emptyset$ and $\lim_{k \to +\infty} \Theta(u_{k}) = \min \Theta$ . Therefore, there exist $r \in R$ and R > 0 such that the set $\Gamma_{r}^{R}$ contains $(u_{k})$ and is relatively compact for the strong topology. A standard argument shows that $(u_{k})$ converges strongly as $k \to +\infty$ . [Every subsequence has a further strongly convergent subsequence by relative compactness. Its strong limit is also its weak limit, hence equals the given weak limit; the usual subsequence criterion then gives strong convergence of the full sequence.] ☐
items.remark: [Prove hint: relative compactness gives a strongly convergent subsequence; weak-limit uniqueness identifies its limit]

items.name: Corollary 9
items.statement: COROLLARY 9. Let $H$ be finite-dimensional. Assume Hypothesis $H$ holds and $S \neq \emptyset$ . Then $(u_k)$ converges to an element of $S$ .
items.proof: [In finite dimension, weak convergence is equivalent to strong convergence. Hypothesis $H_\Psi$ gives continuity of $\nabla\Psi$, hence weak-to-weak sequential continuity, so Theorem 1 applies and yields convergence to an element of $S$.]
items.remark: [Note: in finite dimension weak and strong convergence coincide]

external_theorems.name: Opial's Lemma
external_theorems.statement: Let $(x_n)$ be a sequence in a Hilbert space and let $S\ne\emptyset$. If (a) for every $q\in S$, $\lim_n\|x_n-q\|$ exists, and (b) every weak sequential cluster point of $(x_n)$ belongs to $S$, then $(x_n)$ converges weakly to an element of $S$.
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: Z. Opial, “Weak convergence of the sequence of successive approximations for nonexpansive mappings,” *Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.* 73 (1967), 591–597.

external_theorems.name: Descent lemma for a Lipschitz gradient
external_theorems.statement: If $\Psi:H\to\mathbf{R}$ is differentiable and $\nabla\Psi$ is $L_\Psi$-Lipschitz, then for all $x,v\in H$, $$\Psi(v)\leq\Psi(x)+\langle\nabla\Psi(x),v-x\rangle+\frac{L_\Psi}{2}\|v-x\|^2.$$
external_theorems.proof: Cited from: D. Bertsekas, *Nonlinear Programming*, Proposition A.24 (1999); J. M. Ortega and W. C. Rheinboldt, *Iterative Solution of Nonlinear Equations in Several Variables* (2000).
external_theorems.remark: [Prove hint: apply the standard smoothness/descent inequality with $x=u_k$ and $v=u_{k+1}$]
